breaking.headline: Anthropic’s first trade prints at $111.50, then slips under $100
breaking.fact: Anthropic opened on the Nasdaq at $111.50 a share Thursday — 34% above its $83 IPO price, putting the Claude maker’s fully diluted value near $2 trillion in the largest IPO on record — then pared the gain and slipped below $100 in the first hour of trading, last around $97.17. The company sold 980 million shares at $83, raising $81.3 billion; Sean was allocated 66 shares at the IPO price.

breaking.headline: Stocks give back the morning pop; S&P heads for a sixth straight loss
breaking.fact: The Nasdaq opened up nearly 2% on Anthropic’s debut and the S&P 500 rose about 1% in early trade, but both turned sharply lower by the afternoon: the S&P 500 is down about 2% at 7,175.88, a sixth straight daily loss, the Nasdaq is down about 2.3% and the Dow is off about 2.2%, with the VIX up near 28.

breaking.headline: Walmart beats estimates and raises its outlook — shares fall anyway
breaking.fact: Walmart reported third-quarter adjusted earnings of $0.65 a share on revenue of $188.8 billion, both ahead of Wall Street’s estimates, and raised its full-year sales growth outlook to 4.9%–5.2% and adjusted earnings to $2.84–$2.89 a share. U.S. e-commerce sales jumped 23%, but the shares still fell about 1.5% in morning trade as the raised outlook came in below some analysts’ hopes.

breaking.headline: Jobless claims rise to 203,000, above the 198,000 expected
breaking.fact: Initial jobless claims rose to a seasonally adjusted 203,000 in the week ended November 14, up 1,000 from the prior week after revision and above the 198,000 economists expected; the four-week moving average rose 2,000 to 197,750.

weekInBrief.headline: Health insurers plunge as CMS proposes sweeping Medicare Advantage audits
weekInBrief.body: UnitedHealth fell 10.21% and Humana about 13% on Wednesday as managed-care stocks sold off for a second straight day after the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services proposed its CRUSH rule on November 16, which would let the agency apply audit error rates across whole Medicare Advantage contracts and claw back overpayments, targeting nearly $90 billion in federal savings over a decade. UnitedHealth alone accounted for about two-fifths of the Dow’s 561-point drop; the rule is only a proposal, with comments due January 19, 2027.

weekInBrief.headline: Palo Alto Networks jumps about 10% on a strong quarter and a $4.5 billion AI deal
weekInBrief.body: Palo Alto Networks reported fiscal first-quarter revenue of $3.44 billion, up 39% year over year, with next-generation security annual recurring revenue up 66% to $9.73 billion, and raised its full-year revenue outlook to $14.52–$14.57 billion. The company also agreed to acquire AI startup AppliedCompute in an all-stock deal valued at about $4.5 billion; the shares rose about 10% after hours and kept climbing Thursday.

weekInBrief.headline: Gold slides to $3,719, its lowest since September 2025
weekInBrief.body: Gold fell intraday to $3,719.55 an ounce on Wednesday, its lowest since September 2025, as a firm dollar — at its highest in 19 months — and 10-year yields above 5% drained the safe-haven trade; U.S. gold futures closed down 3.2% at $3,741.90. Gold is now more than 30% below January’s record above $5,400, with silver under $46.

weekInBrief.headline: Brent slides under $91 as the crude selloff extends
weekInBrief.body: Brent crude fell about 2% to roughly $90 a barrel in Thursday trade, extending Wednesday’s roughly 5% plunge after U.S. crude stockpiles jumped 5.28 million barrels in the week to November 13. WTI held near $83. Both benchmarks are on pace for monthly declines of roughly 20% even as the U.S. naval blockade keeps Iranian crude exports near a standstill.

items.headline: Latest from the Strait
items.body: TankerTrackers.com reported on Thursday that Iran appears to be positioning itself to resume oil shipments after months under the U.S. naval blockade, a move the blockade’s new enforcement rules are designed to stop: CENTCOM’s Wednesday advisory warns that any vessel taking Iranian cargo in a ship-to-ship transfer may be stopped, boarded, diverted or seized, even if it never enters Iranian waters. TankerTrackers also reports Iranian crude production plunged 46% in October to about 1.86 million barrels a day, below the country’s pre-war domestic refinery consumption. On oil, the blockade still holds — Iranian crude exports have remained near a standstill for months, shipping sources told Reuters, while Kpler puts total oil and product flows through the strait at about 8.3 million barrels a day in the week to November 11, roughly 48% of pre-war levels.

space.headline: Voyager 1 reaches one full light-day from Earth
space.body: NASA’s Voyager 1 has crossed one full light-day from Earth — about 16.1 billion miles — the farthest any human-made object has ever traveled. Launched in 1977, the probe is still sending data back from interstellar space, nearly 50 years after it left Earth.

space.headline: Rocket Lab flies its 100th Electron launch
space.body: Rocket Lab has now flown 100 Electron launches, a milestone for the small-launch company that has become the workhorse of the light-lift market. The achievement comes as its reusable Neutron rocket’s first launch has slipped into 2027.

space.headline: Astronomers find a triple-star system just 28 light-years away
space.body: Astronomers have discovered a remarkable triple-star system just 28 light-years from Earth — the closest known triple system containing two white dwarfs. Named Welopōʻai, it pairs a red dwarf with a closely orbiting white dwarf, plus a second white dwarf circling the pair at a much greater distance. The team, led by the Université de Montréal, spotted the system with the SPIRou instrument in Hawaii and confirmed it with the Gemini North telescope; the discovery is published in Astronomy & Astrophysics.

space.headline: A gut bacterium’s sugar may help burn harmful visceral fat
space.body: Scientists have found that a sugar produced by a gut bacterium, Clostridium immunis, can increase energy burning in visceral fat — the harmful fat around internal organs — while reducing weight gain and improving metabolic health in animal studies. The Duke-NUS and Duke University team, publishing in Cell Host & Microbe, has filed a patent and is now planning clinical trials in the U.S. to test whether targeting the bacterium could treat obesity.

apod.title: El Niño Rains Paint the Atacama
apod.credit: NASA Earth Observatory images by Michala Garrison, using Landsat data from the U.S. Geological Survey — NASA Earth Observatory Image of the Day, November 19, 2026
apod.explanation: Parts of Chile’s Atacama Desert, normally one of the driest places on Earth, turned red-purple, green and white in austral spring 2026 after an unusually wet winter woke dormant seeds — what scientists say may be the most extensive ‘flowering desert’ of the satellite era. This Landsat 9 view from October 24 shows vast blooms of pata de guanaco southwest of Copiapó, near Desierto Florido National Park.
